Comment: A trial of the SPFresh example at Wikipedia scale on the lab server, before the CloudLab runs: the first two minor batches of the 2026-02 diff (b4x5: 775K inserts and about 744K deletes each), each followed by SPFresh's maintenance as a major epoch (split, merge as SPFresh's paper, reassign of the 64 nearest lists, old copies dropped), on the index with RNG-pruned replicas and its 4-node warmup snapshot (experiment.wiki-c1024-rng-warmup-4.json), inserts routed by the RNG rule. It checks that the epochs run at this scale and measures them (updates.json: decide and apply times, splits, merges, reassigned vectors, the graph patch), so that the CloudLab runs' spacing and SplitLen can be set; its timings are the lab's, not CloudLab's. SplitLen 400, MergeLen 5 and MajorMax 1300 are the update experiment's (experiment.wiki-c1024-cloudlab-gpu-updates.json): on this index only 22 lists are longer than 400 (930 on the base), so its epochs split what the batches grow. CPU backend (the GPUs are other users'), 8 CPUs and 24 GB a node, no read limit, a low load of 200 q/s. No version ground truth on the lab: recall holds until the first batch flips. The work directory is on /netsys, which has room for the nodes' copies of the snapshot's raw files (78 GiB; /data-ssd had 109 GB free after the warmup): it holds copies of the index's assignment and partitions (assign-gp-64.bin and partitions/ from /data-ssd/chenxu/work/wiki-c1024-rng, with their stage records), so the snapshot, keyed by content, is found.
